name: slopcheck
tagline: Paste a URL or a screenshot to flag AI-generated design patterns
description:
slopcheck is a web tool that looks for AI-generated design patterns. The page says you paste a link or drop a screenshot, and it reads the markup and the pixels. It says screenshots never leave the browser, with a limit of PNG, JPG, or WebP up to 12 MB. It says links are read through r.jina.ai and photographed by microlink, and that a second opinion is written by an AI through OpenRouter. It says nothing is stored.

No account, price, or license was on the page. The page calls the result "Not science."
pricing_detail: No price or account was on the page.
agent_guidance:
Use slopcheck as a second pair of eyes on a page that might be using stock AI layout patterns. Paste a URL, or drop a screenshot if the page should stay on the machine. The site says screenshots stay in the browser and that links are fetched through r.jina.ai and microlink.

The page says the result is not science, and that the written roast comes from a model through OpenRouter. Do not treat the output as an audit. No license was stated.
why_it_matters: It names the visual tells of generated marketing pages, which is a review step most galleries do not do.
tier_reason: The inputs, the privacy claim, and the model path are on the page. License and a method are not.
evidence: Checked https://ai-slop-checker.vercel.app/ on 2026-10-25. The page states the inputs, the 12 MB limit, the third-party readers, the OpenRouter line, and that nothing is stored. No price or license was on the page. Source tweet: https://x.com/buildwithsid/status/2108552341939266028.
